title: CMS determines that Viz.ai ContaCT is a substantial clinical improvement because it shortens stroke-specialist notification, and approves add-on payments
summary: CMS found that Viz.ai ContaCT shortens time to specialist notification for large vessel occlusion stroke; in routine use the median time to notification was 4.31 minutes.
account: Viz.ai applied to the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS) for a new technology add-on payment for ContaCT, software that reads CT angiograms of the brain and alerts a stroke specialist to a suspected large vessel occlusion. ContaCT became commercially available in October 2018. In the proposed rule, CMS questioned whether the evidence showed that shorter notification times improve outcomes, and the company then submitted more data. In a retrospective test on past scans that supported its FDA authorization, the mean time from scan to specialist notification was 7.32 minutes with ContaCT and 58.72 minutes in usual care. Viz.ai reported that across 4,763 patients in six months of routine use, the median time to notification was 4.31 minutes. Unpublished single-center reviews at hospitals in Colorado, Georgia and Tennessee reported average reductions in door-to-puncture time of 24, 30 and 44 minutes, and a Mount Sinai cohort of 42 thrombectomy patients had lower stroke severity scores after implementation. In the final rule published on 18 September 2020, CMS determined that ContaCT represents a substantial clinical improvement because it shortens time to notification, and it approved add-on payments for fiscal year 2021. CMS based its finding on information that the applicant provided, and the hospital comparisons were small single-site cohorts.
purpose: ContaCT was built to alert a stroke specialist to a suspected large vessel occlusion in parallel with the usual radiology read. Faster notification is that purpose.
system: ContaCT (Viz LVO algorithm with Viz Hub and Viz View)
deployer: US hospitals using ContaCT, including SkyRidge Medical Center, Wellstar, Methodist Le Bonheur Healthcare and Mount Sinai Health System
